titre: Exercices — Discours rapporté et concordance des temps
consigne: Cherche chaque exercice au brouillon avant d'ouvrir le corrigé.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I feel sick », she said.
corrige: Introducteur au passé → backshift ; présent feel → prétérit felt.
She said she felt sick.
exercices.reponse: She said she felt sick.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I have lost my keys and I can't find them », he said.
corrige: have lost → past perfect : had lost.
can't → couldn't ; them reste them.
He said he had lost his keys and couldn't find them.
exercices.reponse: He said he had lost his keys and couldn't find them.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte en adaptant les repères : « I'll finish it tomorrow », she said yesterday.
corrige: will → would ; tomorrow → the next day.
She said she would finish it the next day.
exercices.reponse: She said she would finish it the next day.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte la question : « What time does the film start? », he asked.
corrige: Question ouverte → ask + mot interrogatif + ordre affirmatif, sans do.
does start → started (backshift).
He asked what time the film started.
exercices.reponse: He asked what time the film started.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « Do you speak French? », she asked me.
corrige: Question fermée → if/whether.
do you speak → I spoke (backshift, ordre affirmatif).
She asked me if I spoke French.
exercices.reponse: She asked me if I spoke French.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte l'ordre : « Close the window, please », he said.
corrige: Ordre → tell/ask + complément + to + BV.
He asked me to close the window.
exercices.reponse: He asked me to close the window.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « Don't be late again! », the teacher said.
corrige: Ordre négatif → not to + BV.
The teacher told us not to be late again.
exercices.reponse: The teacher told us not to be late again.

exercices.enonce: Corrige les fautes : « He said me that he will call me tomorrow. » (introducteur au passé)
corrige: said me → told me (ou said to me).
will → would ; tomorrow → the next day.
He told me that he would call me the next day.
exercices.reponse: He told me that he would call me the next day.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « You must wear a helmet and you can borrow mine », the instructor said.
corrige: must → had to ; can → could.
mine (« le mien », celui de l'instructeur) devient his ou hers selon que l'instructeur est un homme ou une femme.
The instructor said I had to wear a helmet and could borrow his (ou hers).
exercices.reponse: The instructor said I had to wear a helmet and could borrow his (ou hers).

exercices.enonce: Rapporte le dialogue : « I saw this film last week and I really enjoyed it », she told me.
corrige: saw → had seen ; this → that ; last week → the week before.
enjoyed → had enjoyed ; it reste it.
She told me she had seen that film the week before and had really enjoyed it.
exercices.reponse: She told me she had seen that film the week before and had really enjoyed it.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I live in London », he said.
corrige: Introducteur au passé (said) → backshift : présent live → prétérit lived.
I devient he.
exercices.reponse: He said he lived in London.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « We are hungry », they said.
corrige: are → were (présent → prétérit).
We devient they.
exercices.reponse: They said they were hungry.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I missed the bus », she said.
corrige: Prétérit missed → past perfect had missed.
I devient she.
exercices.reponse: She said she had missed the bus.

exercices.enonce: Donne la forme rapportée (après un introducteur au passé) de chaque modal : may, can, will.
corrige: may → might.
can → could ; will → would.
exercices.reponse: might, could, would

exercices.enonce: Donne l'équivalent en discours rapporté de : today, here, now.
corrige: Les repères reculent vers le passé.
today → that day ; here → there ; now → then.
exercices.reponse: that day, there, then

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I have never been to Scotland », he said.
corrige: Present perfect have been → past perfect had been.
never garde sa place, entre had et been.
exercices.reponse: He said he had never been to Scotland.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I'm watching a documentary », my brother said.
corrige: am → was : le présent en be + -ing devient was + -ing.
I devient he.
exercices.reponse: My brother said he was watching a documentary.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I can't come to the party », Tom said.
corrige: can't → couldn't.
I devient he.
exercices.reponse: Tom said he couldn't come to the party.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « It may rain this afternoon », the forecaster said.
corrige: may → might.
this → that : this afternoon devient that afternoon.
exercices.reponse: The forecaster said it might rain that afternoon.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I bought this jacket two days ago », Emma said.
corrige: bought → had bought ; this → that.
ago → before : two days ago devient two days before.
exercices.reponse: Emma said she had bought that jacket two days before.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte la question : « Why are you crying? », his mother asked him.
corrige: Question ouverte : asked + why + sujet + verbe, ordre affirmatif, sans point d'interrogation.
are you crying → he was crying.
exercices.reponse: His mother asked him why he was crying.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte la question : « Have you finished your homework? », Dad asked me.
corrige: Question fermée → if ou whether.
have you finished → I had finished (ordre affirmatif, past perfect) ; your → my.
exercices.reponse: Dad asked me if (ou whether) I had finished my homework.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte l'ordre : « Open your books », the teacher said to the pupils.
corrige: Ordre → tell + complément + to + BV.
your devient their (les livres des élèves).
exercices.reponse: The teacher told the pupils to open their books.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec « said » ou « told » : (a) « She ___ me she was busy. » (b) « She ___ she was busy. »
corrige: tell exige un complément de personne : told me.
say s'emploie sans complément de personne : said.
exercices.reponse: (a) told (b) said

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « Don't touch the paintings », the guide said to the visitors.
corrige: Ordre négatif → tell + complément + not to + BV.
Don't touch devient not to touch.
exercices.reponse: The guide told the visitors not to touch the paintings.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « How long have you been waiting? », he asked me.
corrige: Question ouverte : ordre affirmatif après how long.
have you been waiting → I had been waiting (past perfect).
exercices.reponse: He asked me how long I had been waiting.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « Will you help me? », Anna asked Paul.
corrige: Question fermée → if ou whether ; will → would.
you désigne Paul (he) et me désigne Anna (her).
exercices.reponse: Anna asked Paul if (ou whether) he would help her.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « You must be home before ten », my parents said.
corrige: must (obligation) → had to.
You désigne ici la personne qui parle : I.
exercices.reponse: My parents said I had to be home before ten.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte la question : « Shall I open the door? », he asked.
corrige: Question fermée → if ou whether.
shall → should ; ordre affirmatif : he should open.
exercices.reponse: He asked if (ou whether) he should open the door.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I'll see you here tomorrow », she said to me.
corrige: said to me → told me ; will → would.
here → there ; tomorrow → the next day (ou the following day).
exercices.reponse: She told me she would see me there the next day.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte en utilisant le verbe « admit » : « I broke the vase », he said.
corrige: admit = reconnaître, avouer : il remplace say.
broke → had broken (prétérit → past perfect). On accepte aussi : He admitted breaking the vase.
exercices.reponse: He admitted (that) he had broken the vase.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte en utilisant le verbe « promise » : « I'll be careful, I promise », she said.
corrige: Le verbe promise reprend l'idée de promesse : inutile de répéter « I promise ».
will → would. On accepte aussi : She promised to be careful.
exercices.reponse: She promised (that) she would be careful.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la phrase : « She asked me where did I go. »
corrige: Dans une question rapportée, on n'emploie pas did et on garde l'ordre affirmatif.
went recule au past perfect : had gone.
exercices.reponse: She asked me where I had gone.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la phrase : « He asked me I was ready. »
corrige: C'est une question fermée rapportée : il manque if ou whether.
He asked me if I was ready.
exercices.reponse: He asked me if (ou whether) I was ready.

exercices.enonce: Retrouve les paroles exactes : « He said he had lost his wallet. »
corrige: had lost peut venir d'un prétérit (lost) ou d'un present perfect (have lost).
he devient I et his devient my. Les deux réponses sont correctes.
exercices.reponse: « I lost my wallet. » ou « I have lost my wallet. »

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I'm busy now, but I can call you tonight », she told me.
corrige: am → was ; can → could ; now → then.
tonight → that night ; you devient me.
exercices.reponse: She told me she was busy then, but (that) she could call me that night.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « We visited this museum yesterday and we loved it », they said.
corrige: visited / loved → had visited / had loved (on peut ne pas répéter had).
this → that ; yesterday → the day before.
exercices.reponse: They said they had visited that museum the day before and had loved it.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « What will you do after the exam? », my friend asked me.
corrige: Question ouverte → ordre affirmatif : what I would do.
will → would ; you devient I.
exercices.reponse: My friend asked me what I would do after the exam.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « Water boils at 100 °C », the teacher explained. Faut-il reculer le temps ?
corrige: C'est une vérité générale, toujours vraie : on peut garder le présent.
Le backshift (boiled) n'est pas une faute, mais le présent est ici le plus naturel.
exercices.reponse: The teacher explained that water boils at 100 °C.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte la demande : « Please call me when you arrive », my mother said.
corrige: Demande polie → ask + complément + to + BV.
me devient her ; arrive recule : when I arrived.
exercices.reponse: My mother asked me to call her when I arrived.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la phrase : « He told that he was sorry. »
corrige: tell exige un complément de personne.
Deux corrections possibles : He said that he was sorry. / He told me that he was sorry.
exercices.reponse: He said that he was sorry. (ou He told me that he was sorry.)

exercices.enonce: Retrouve la question directe : « She asked me whether I had ever been to Ireland. »
corrige: whether indique une question fermée (réponse yes / no).
had been → have been ; on rétablit l'inversion : Have you … ?
exercices.reponse: « Have you ever been to Ireland? »

exercices.enonce: Rapporte en utilisant le verbe « warn » : « Be careful, the road is icy », he said to us.
corrige: warn = avertir, mettre en garde ; il exige un complément (warn us).
is → was. On accepte aussi : He warned us to be careful because the road was icy.
exercices.reponse: He warned us (that) the road was icy.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I can't sleep. Can you turn the music down? », Lucy said to her neighbour, Mr Smith.
corrige: Première phrase : told + can't → couldn't.
Deuxième phrase : demande → asked him to + BV (ou asked him if he could turn the music down).
exercices.reponse: Lucy told Mr Smith she couldn't sleep and asked him to turn the music down.

exercices.enonce: Ben m'a dit hier : « I'll phone you tomorrow. I must go now. » Rapporte ses paroles.
corrige: will → would ; tomorrow → the next day.
must → had to ; now → then ; on relie par and (that).
exercices.reponse: Ben told me he would phone me the next day and that he had to go then.

exercices.enonce: Corrige les deux fautes : « He asked me where was the station and told me don't worry. »
corrige: Question rapportée : ordre affirmatif → where the station was.
Ordre négatif rapporté : not to + BV → told me not to worry.
exercices.reponse: He asked me where the station was and told me not to worry.

exercices.enonce: Une journaliste a demandé à une scientifique, Sarah Jones : « Are you optimistic? Do you think the treatment will work? » Rapporte les deux questions.
corrige: Questions fermées → if (ou whether), ordre affirmatif, sans do.
are → was ; think → thought ; will → would.
exercices.reponse: The journalist asked Sarah Jones if she was optimistic and if she thought the treatment would work.

exercices.enonce: Retrouve les paroles exactes de l'entraîneur : « The coach told the players not to give up and said they could still win. »
corrige: not to give up vient d'un ordre négatif : Don't give up!
they could still win → You can still win (could → can, they → you).
exercices.reponse: « Don't give up! You can still win. »

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I met Tom here last year », she said.
corrige: met → had met ; here → there.
last year → the year before (ou the previous year).
exercices.reponse: She said she had met Tom there the year before.

exercices.enonce: Rapporte : « I've just finished my essay. I'm going to send it to my teacher today », Mia said.
corrige: have just finished → had just finished ; am going to → was going to.
my → her ; today → that day.
exercices.reponse: Mia said she had just finished her essay and was going to send it to her teacher that day.
